    for (const auto& w : walls) {

This flat list is the simplest possible representation — no BSP tree, no spatial acceleration, no scene graph. For a small arena (<50 walls) the GPU overdraw is negligible and the CPU cost is zero.

Lambda Helper Pattern

Constructing many MapWall entries with the same height and tile-scale would be repetitive. A local lambda reduces noise:

const float kTS  = 6.0f;  // tile scale for wall texture
const float kFTS = 1.5f;  // tile scale for floor/ceiling

    return { Vec3{cx, kWH, cz}, hx, kWH, hz, tex, sf::Color::White, kTS };
};
Lambda default-argument rule: local constexpr variables cannot appear as default arguments in lambda parameters — this is a C++ limitation. The fix is to capture them and use them directly in the lambda body (as shown above).

To add a new room or obstacle, add a MapWall entry to buildMapWalls():

No spatial index update is needed — the flat list is rebuilt once and used until the game ends.

  • AABB — Axis-Aligned Bounding Box: a box with edges parallel to world axes, defined by centre + half-extents.
  • Half-extent — the distance from the centre to a face along one axis (hx, hy, hz); the full width is 2×half-extent.
  • MapWall — the project's AABB descriptor struct, carrying geometry, texture, tint, and tile scale.
  • drawTexturedBox — renders one MapWall by computing 8 vertices and issuing 6 quads in immediate-mode OpenGL.

Zone-Based Enemy Spawning

Issue #6Game designSpawn systems

This lesson covers how to constrain enemy spawning to named map zones, how to prevent enemies from spawning on top of the player, and how to cap retry loops so the game never hangs regardless of player position.

Why Random-Anywhere Spawning Breaks Gameplay

Spawning enemies anywhere in the arena produces three problems:

  • Surprise teleports: an enemy appears 1 metre in front of the player with no warning.
  • Layout ignorance: enemies spawn in corners, behind walls, or off the intended fight path.
  • Exploitability: experienced players learn there is no safe retreat — every position is equally dangerous.

Zone-based spawning fixes all three: enemies appear in designer-chosen areas that match the map's intended flow, never too close to the player, and never in inaccessible geometry.

The SpawnZone Rectangle

struct SpawnZone {
    float minX, maxX;
    float minZ, maxZ;
};

// A-site (far positive-X / negative-Z corner)
inline SpawnZone aSpawnZone() { return SpawnZone{ 30.0f,  70.0f, -70.0f, -20.0f }; }

// B-site (far positive-Z corner)
inline SpawnZone bSpawnZone() { return SpawnZone{-20.0f,  20.0f,  30.0f,  70.0f }; }

Y-position is always set to 3.0f (enemy eye height above the floor), so only X and Z are sampled from the zone rectangle.

The Retry Cap Pattern

The naive approach — loop until a valid position is found — can hang if the player occupies all possible spawn positions. The fix is a retry cap with a failure sentinel: 

/** Returns alive=false if no valid position found after 50 attempts. */
Enemy spawnEnemy(int wave, const Vec3& playerPos) {
    constexpr int   kMaxSpawnRetries = 50;
    constexpr float kMinPlayerDistSq = 30.0f * 30.0f;

    Enemy enemy{};
    enemy.headingDeg    = randomFloat(0.0f, 360.0f);
    enemy.shootCooldown = randomFloat(0.35f, 1.1f);

    for (int attempt = 0; attempt < kMaxSpawnRetries; ++attempt) {
        // Pick A or B site with equal probability each attempt
        const SpawnZone zone = (randomFloat(0.0f, 1.0f) < 0.5f)
                             ? aSpawnZone() : bSpawnZone();
        const float px = randomFloat(zone.minX, zone.maxX);
        const float pz = randomFloat(zone.minZ, zone.maxZ);
        const float dx = px - playerPos.x;
        const float dz = pz - playerPos.z;
        if (dx * dx + dz * dz >= kMinPlayerDistSq) {
            enemy.pos   = Vec3{px, 3.0f, pz};
            enemy.alive = true;
            return enemy;
        }
    }

    enemy.alive = false;   // retry cap hit
    return enemy;
}

Caller-Side Handling

The call site in updateEnemies() checks the sentinel and breaks out of the spawn loop for this frame — it retries next frame: 

while (aliveCount < desiredAliveEnemies(game) && game.enemiesRemainingToSpawn > 0) {
    Enemy enemy = spawnEnemy(game.wave, game.player.pos);
    if (!enemy.alive) {
        break;   // cap hit — try again next frame when player has moved
    }
    game.enemies.push_back(enemy);
    --game.enemiesRemainingToSpawn;
    ++aliveCount;
}
Break vs continue: break exits the spawn loop entirely for this frame. continue would retry immediately in the same frame — and if all 50 retries fail again every iteration, you still hang. break is correct because the player will almost certainly have moved by next frame (16ms at 60fps).

Design Decisions

DecisionValueReason
Retry cap50 attemptsFar exceeds normal cases; fast enough to run every frame
Min player distance30 units (sq: 900)Greater than the 22-unit original; gives player reaction time
Zone selection50/50 A or B per attemptEqual pressure on both sites matches CSGO's attack pattern
Distance checkSquared distance (dx²+dz²)Avoids sqrt(); equivalent to circular exclusion
Squared distance trick: comparing dx*dx + dz*dz >= radius*radius is cheaper than comparing sqrt(dx*dx + dz*dz) >= radius. The result is identical — use it whenever the goal is "is the distance at least R?" without needing the actual distance value.

Key Vocabulary

  • SpawnZone — a named axis-aligned rectangle (minX, maxX, minZ, maxZ) defining where enemies may appear.
  • Retry cap — a maximum number of attempts in a spawn loop; prevents infinite loops when all positions are blocked.
  • alive sentinel — a boolean field on the return value used to signal "spawn failed" when the retry cap is exceeded. The caller checks it before using the struct.
  • Player exclusion radius — a minimum distance from the player required before a spawn position is accepted; protects against insta-kill spawns.
  • Squared distance comparison — comparing dx²+dz² against r² instead of computing sqrt; a common optimisation for range checks.
  • Break-on-failure — exiting the spawn loop when capped, deferring retries to the next frame; preferred over spinning in the same frame.

Vocabulary: Zone-Based Enemy Spawning

Key terms from Issue #6 — constrained spawning, retry caps, and sentinel patterns.

SpawnZone
An axis-aligned rectangle (minX, maxX, minZ, maxZ) defining where enemies are permitted to appear. Separates the concept of "valid spawn area" from the spawning algorithm itself.
In cpp_shooter_game: aSpawnZone() (X: 30–70, Z: −70 to −20) and bSpawnZone() (X: −20–20, Z: 30–70) in map.hpp.
Usage: "Define spawn zones once in map.hpp — the spawner doesn't need to know map geometry, only which zone to sample."
Retry cap
A hard upper bound on the number of spawn attempts made in a single function call. Prevents the spawner from looping indefinitely when all positions in a zone are blocked by the player exclusion radius.
In cpp_shooter_game: kMaxSpawnRetries = 50 — 50 attempts before the spawn is abandoned for this frame.
Usage: "Always pair a retry loop with a cap. A loop without a cap is a potential hang — even a 1-in-a-million scenario becomes common at 60fps over many minutes."
alive sentinel
A boolean field on a return struct used to communicate "this value is invalid — the operation failed." The caller must check it before using the struct's other fields. An alternative to returning an optional or throwing an exception.
In cpp_shooter_game: enemy.alive = false signals retry cap hit; the caller's if (!enemy.alive) break; skips the slot.
Usage: "The sentinel pattern is clean when the failure case needs no explanation — just check alive before push_back."
Player exclusion radius
A minimum distance from the player that a spawn position must exceed before it is accepted. Prevents enemies from appearing immediately in the player's face with no reaction time.
In cpp_shooter_game: kMinPlayerDistSq = 30.0f * 30.0f = 900.0f; 30 world units compared via squared distance.
Usage: "Set the exclusion radius to at least the distance a player can see clearly — 30 units gives one to two seconds of reaction time at normal enemy speed."
Squared distance comparison
Comparing dx²+dz² against r² instead of sqrt(dx²+dz²) against r. Mathematically equivalent for "is the distance at least r?" but avoids the expensive sqrt() call.
In cpp_shooter_game: dx*dx + dz*dz >= kMinPlayerDistSq in the spawn retry loop.
Usage: "Use squared distance for any per-frame range check where you only need to know 'closer than / farther than' — it's a ubiquitous micro-optimisation in game code."

SpawnZone
An axis-aligned rectangle (minX, maxX, minZ, maxZ) defining where enemies are permitted to appear. Separates the concept of "valid spawn area" from the spawning algorithm itself.

Retry cap
A hard upper bound on the number of spawn attempts made in a single function call. Prevents the spawner from looping indefinitely when all positions in a zone are blocked by the player exclusion radius.
In cpp_shooter_game: kMaxSpawnRetries = 50 — 50 attempts before the spawn is abandoned for this frame.

## Summary
All 6 `ready-for-ai` issues from the CSGO overhaul plan were implemented successfully.
The game now has enemy aim spread, a magazine/reload system, first/third-person camera
toggle, procedural textures, CSGO-style corridor map geometry, and zone-based enemy
spawning. All 6 draft PRs are open and awaiting review.

## Completed ✅
| Issue | Title | Branch | PR | Concept Taught |
|-------|-------|--------|----|----------------|
| #1 | Enemy aim spread — per-type miss chance | feature/issue-1-enemy-aim-spread | #7 | Angular spread / aim perturbation |

|---------|--------|-------|-------|
| Angular spread in FPS AI (#1) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Magazine/reserve ammo state machines (#2) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| First/third-person camera toggle (#3) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Procedural texture generation / Wang hash (#4) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| AABB map geometry for FPS levels (#5) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Zone-based enemy spawning (#6) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |

Total: 18 HTML files + index.html → `docs/learning/`

## Test Status
Build passes cleanly on all 6 branches (`make -j4` with SFML 2.5.1 / CMake 3.20+).
No automated gameplay tests exist yet — see "Suggested First Move" below.

## Notable Technical Findings
- **SFML version:** Only 2.5.1 is installed; CMakeLists.txt was adjusted from 2.6 to 2.5.
- **Anonymous namespace include rule:** Headers that forward-declare functions defined inside
  main.cpp's anonymous namespace MUST be `#include`'d inside that namespace, after the
  function is defined. Violation causes `undefined reference` linker errors. Applied to
  both `textures_proc.hpp` (#4) and `map.hpp` (#5).
- **Lambda default-argument rule:** Local `constexpr` variables cannot be used as lambda
  parameter default arguments in C++. Fixed in #5 by capturing and using them in the body.
- **Spawn system:** Issue #6 raises the player exclusion radius from 22 to 30 units and
  moves the distance check inside `spawnEnemy()` itself (with a 50-attempt retry cap),
  eliminating the old `continue` loop that could hang if the player occupied the arena
  centre.

## Suggested First Move
Run the game interactively and verify the two highest-risk changes:
1. **Issue #5 map geometry (PR #11):** Walk through all five zones (T-Spawn, Mid, A-Site,
   B-Corridor, B-Site) and confirm wall layout matches the intended CSGO layout.
2. **Issue #6 spawning (PR #12):** Watch enemy spawn positions across a full wave — they
   should only appear in the A-site (positive-X) or B-site (positive-Z) corners, never
   near the map centre or the player spawn.

Overnight session complete. Here's a summary of what was accomplished:

---

## Overnight Session Complete

**All 6 issues implemented. 6 draft PRs open. 18 learning files generated.**

| PR | Issue | Concept |
|----|-------|---------|
| #7 | #1 Enemy aim spread | Angular spread / aim perturbation |
| #8 | #2 Ammo/reload system | Magazine + reserve state machine |
| #9 | #3 Camera toggle | FPS/TPS eye position, rising-edge detection |
| #10 | #4 Procedural textures | Wang hash noise, bilinear smooth noise |
| #11 | #5 CSGO corridor map | AABB flat wall list, room layout |
| #12 | #6 Zone-based spawning | SpawnZone rectangles, retry cap, alive sentinel |

**Suggested first move:** Open `OVERNIGHT_REPORT.md` for the full findings, then start with PRs #11 (map geometry) and #12 (zone spawning) — those are the two most impactful to verify interactively by walking the level and watching enemy spawns.

**Notable technical finding to carry forward:** Any header that forward-declares a function defined inside `main.cpp`'s anonymous namespace must be `#include`'d *inside* that namespace, *after* the function definition — otherwise you get a linker error. This applies to all future `.hpp` files in this project.
